bug_semantics: On self-hosted deployments, PUT /api/global/users/tenant/owner was reachable by any authenticated Budibase user because its only endpoint middleware was cloudRestricted, whose internal-API-key check is skipped when SELF_HOSTED or DISABLE_ACCOUNT_PORTAL is set. The handler trusted attacker-supplied originalEmail, newAccountEmail, and tenantIds, changed the matching tenant user's email, and deliberately saved with isAccountHolder:true and allowChangingEmail:true. A BASIC user could therefore redirect the account-holder/admin identity to an attacker-controlled mailbox and complete takeover through the public password-reset flow where SMTP is configured.
flaw_origin: PR #16485 was squash-landed as 634cfb525888014c770b3671b29fc9f9fdd06dbd. Its first functional member, bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a, simultaneously created changeTenantOwnerEmail, registered the no-tenancy PUT route with cloudRestricted but no role/internal guard, and allowed the account-holder email mutation. Later member 006565aaef3ed33a709ad5237b6e6b3c99bc6dfe merely changed tenant discovery to request-supplied tenantIds, and babad6836ca3e9b26765646f9746f546279eaa0b only fixed a documentation-tag typo; neither is the first writer of the missing-authorization flaw.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file -p bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a` shows author and committer Mel O'Hagan <mel@budibase.com> and only the subject `Change email endpoint for account holder tenant users`; it has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, or bot identity.
evidence: First-party advisory https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/security/advisories/GHSA-j82g-67x3-xcwh states the attack path, identifies the route/controller/middleware, and declares affected `<3.40.0` and patched `3.40.0`. In the validated clone, `git log -S'changeTenantOwnerEmail' -- packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts packages/worker/src/api/routes/global/users.ts` and `git log -L '/export const changeTenantOwnerEmail = async/,+38:packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts'` identify reachable squash 634cfb525888014c770b3671b29fc9f9fdd06dbd as the first landed writer and 58fd7951e09d2617ccc8236b485a6cdc9ace65c6 as the authorization change. The PR patch at https://github.com/Budibase/budibase/pull/16485.patch exposes members bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a, 006565aaef3ed33a709ad5237b6e6b3c99bc6dfe, and babad6836ca3e9b26765646f9746f546279eaa0b. `git cat-file -p` verifies those objects; the first object's parent is 04c24a96a83194c432c2a1de0f211ecb17c14ae4. `git diff 04c24a96a83194c432c2a1de0f211ecb17c14ae4 bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a -- packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts packages/worker/src/api/routes/global/users.ts packages/worker/src/api/index.ts` shows the BIC adding the unguarded handler, cloudRestricted-only route, and no-tenancy exemption; `git grep -n -e changeTenantOwnerEmail -e /api/global/users/tenant/owner 04c24a96a83194c432c2a1de0f211ecb17c14ae4 -- packages/worker/src/api packages/types/src/api/web/user.ts` returns no matches, directly proving parent absence. `git rev-parse babad6836ca3e9b26765646f9746f546279eaa0b^{tree} 634cfb525888014c770b3671b29fc9f9fdd06dbd^{tree}` returns the same tree 8c6a8996ac85643f92bcef4fdf04db68c0834725 for both, proving the squash decomposition. `git show 58fd7951e09d2617ccc8236b485a6cdc9ace65c6 -- packages/worker/src/api/controllers/global/users.ts` adds `if (!ctx.internal) ctx.throw(403, "Unauthorized")` directly before the mutation. Tag ancestry gives a sharper implementation boundary than the advisory: tag 3.13.8 is exactly squash parent 602d831fc4a31f303171d0a18e408b101a7f33ff and lacks the endpoint, while 3.13.9 (045b837d0339969d517ff1b3563c05cb338812e2) contains squash 634cfb525888014c770b3671b29fc9f9fdd06dbd. Tag 3.39.18 (9e0139b7636f9e77ffa7b568373392f55dde9174) contains the vulnerable handler without the internal check; `git tag --contains 58fd7951e09d2617ccc8236b485a6cdc9ace65c6` begins at 3.39.19, and tag 3.39.19 (2cbae01b8850b218eda58d6edf607b27bdbe37fa) contains the guard. Tag 3.40.0 (661fe55d609404d073eea86702e0bde7942c3f10) also contains the fix, confirming the advertised patched boundary while showing that the repository's tagged code was already fixed in 3.39.19.
reasoning: The vulnerable capability did not exist in the member commit's immediate parent and was fully created by bdbef01a399f3624123ff71519a79f5002d0894a, so that atomic PR member is smaller and causally earlier than the GitHub squash aggregate. Its cloudRestricted check protected cloud deployments with an internal key but intentionally became a no-op in self-host mode; absent a role or internal-only check, normal authenticated users passed the router guard and reached an account-holder mutation that bypassed the normal email-change restriction. Commit 58fd7951e09d2617ccc8236b485a6cdc9ace65c6 closes that exact path by requiring ctx.internal before reading the request body. The BIC commit object has a human identity and no AI marker, so under the BIC-only rule the result is NOT_AI regardless of the `.claude` ignore entry included in the patch, PR metadata, or any later commits. The first-party advisory's `<3.40.0` statement is conservative relative to Git history: direct tag/blob checks prove 3.39.18 vulnerable and 3.39.19 guarded, with 3.40.0 also guarded.
